title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse of access, not a failure of the databases themselves. A sheriff's deputy with legitimate credentials is accused of querying law enforcement systems, including Flock, tag readers and GCIC, to track and surveil a woman in Coffee County without her consent. The systems performed as designed and returned the data they held. The failure sits at the point where authorised access met a personal purpose, which is the condition those systems are not built to detect on their own.

The conduct is alleged to have run from April 10 to May 1, 2024, and it surfaced through a Georgia Bureau of Investigation inquiry rather than at the moment of the queries. Catching it earlier would have required something the facts do not describe, such as query auditing tied to a stated case purpose, or a review that flagged lookups about a person with no investigative connection to the officer. The deputy was terminated when the investigation began, which places detection after the misuse rather than during it.

What is not established is guilt. The eight counts are charges returned by indictment, and an indictment is an accusation, not a finding. Rozar was arrested and released on bond, and his arraignment is scheduled, so no court has determined that the conduct occurred. The account of the woman who spoke anonymously is her account, and the reporting comes from a single outlet.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff's deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, has been indicted on eight counts after a Georgia Bureau of Investigation inquiry. The 49-year-old is accused of misusing law enforcement databases and camera systems, including Flock, tag reader, and GCIC, for personal reasons. Prosecutors say he tracked and surveilled a woman in Coffee County without consent between April 10 and May 1, 2024. The charges include four counts of violation of oath, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of license plate data, and one count of stalking. He was terminated when the investigation began.

Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. The woman, who spoke anonymously, said she waited two years for the investigation and hopes her story encourages other women to come forward. She said she did not want to stay silent and wants to move forward. Rozar is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
title_en: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond
